column2: Retain Reuben's firstborn status, ascent to his father's bed, transfer of blessing to Joseph and non-enrollment for firstborn rights. The selected blessing is not replaced by birthright; the repeated he/his sequence remains unresolved rather than making Joseph Reuben's son by explicit naming.
column3: Who is the subject of gave and the referent of each his, and how should the switch between Reuben and Israel be made clear after syntactic review?

column2: Retain Judah's strength among his brethren, a leader from him and Joseph's blessing. Came and belonged supply English predicates to the nominal clauses without an explicit future messianic title or transfer of the blessing to Judah.
Retain the resumed Reuben-firstborn heading and Enoch, Phallous, Arson and Charmi. The repeated heading closes the introductory qualification without adding a new genealogy.
Retain Joel's Semei and Banaia his son, then a separate heading for Goug son of Semei. The selected second Semei connection is not silently made a linear continuation through Banaia.
Retain Micha, Recha and Baal each with his son under the preceding heading. The chain remains distinct from a simple list of Goug's immediate sons.
Retain Beera, deportation by Thaglathphalnasar king of Assour and leadership of Reuben. The royal and territorial forms remain the inherited representation of this selected Greek.
Retain his brethren, ancestral family, enrollments, generations and the ruler Joel followed by Zacharia. The repeated registration categories remain without a supplied census date in this verse.

Retain Balek's lineage through Ozouz, Sama and Joel, and residence in Aroer toward Nabau and Beelmaon. The singular resident remains Balek contextually, without converting the whole clause to an unnamed tribe.
Retain the eastward wilderness approaches from the Euphrates and abundant livestock in Galaad. The difficult directional description is not replaced by a reconstructed territorial boundary.
column3: How does from the river qualify the wilderness approach, and does the singular residence subject represent a larger family group?

column2: Retain Saul's days, war against resident aliens, falling into their hands, tent dwelling and the eastern extent. The selected paroikoi is not replaced by Hagarenes merely because that group appears later.
column3: Which group is described by the nominative dwelling participle, and how does the compressed as far as all phrase delimit the settlement?

column2: Retain Gad's opposite residence in Basan as far as Selcha. The place names are not converted to modern geography or supplied tribal borders.
Retain Joel firstborn, Sapham second and Jani the scribe in Basan. The selected firstborn designation and explicit scribal office are not replaced by a different chief/list construction.
Retain seven named brethren in their ancestral houses: Michael through Obed. The stated seven matches this list without importing another branch.
Retain the full lineage from Abichail through Uri, Jidai, Galaad, Michael, Isai, Jouri and Zaboucham. The sentence continues into the following unit rather than ending at Zaboucham.
Retain son of Abdiel son of Gouni and ruler of an ancestral house. The title's attachment remains provisional; no missing personal name is supplied before son of Abdiel.
column3: Does the ruler title identify the immediate final ancestor or the subject introduced at the beginning of the lineage?

column2: Retain Galaad, Basan, villages and all Sharon's surrounding region as far as its outlet. The selected exit/outlet expression is not replaced by a named endpoint.
Retain the enrollment of all in the days of both Joatham of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel. The two reign references are not harmonized into a single date.

Retain Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh, military strength, shields, singular sword, drawn bow, training and forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty. The equipment list and exact total remain, with no rounding.
Retain war with Hagarenes, Ituraeans, Naphisaeans and Nadabaeans. The four named opposing groups remain separate.

Retain prevailing, the Hagaraeans and all their tents delivered into their hands, prayer in battle and God's hearing because of hope in Him. Tents follows the selected object rather than being silently changed to allies or troops.

Propose one hundred thousand men for one hundred thousand human lives. The captured persons are expressed by the Greek souls/lives of men construction; men makes clear that this is a captive count alongside captured property, not a death toll, and preserves the male noun. Retain five thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep and two thousand donkeys; the close draft keeps human lives.
Retain many falling wounded, the war from God and settlement in their place until deportation. The casualty expression does not independently classify every fallen person as either surviving or dead.
column3: Does wounded here function broadly as battle casualties, and would slain overstate the selected term?

column2: Retain half Manasseh's range from Basan through Baalermon, Sanir and Mount Aermon and explicit multiplication in Lebanon. The Lebanon clause is not omitted as a geographical difficulty.
Retain all seven ancestral chiefs, their strength, renown and repeated house leadership. The two leadership descriptions remain rather than being collapsed into a single title.

Retain broken faith with the fathers' God and the whoring metaphor for following the expelled peoples' gods. The relative clause is contextually about the peoples God removed; the metaphor is neither embellished nor euphemized.

Retain Israel's God stirring both Phaloch's and Thaglathphalnasar's spirits, Reuben, singular Gaddite and half Manasseh, and Chalach, Chabor and Gozan. The inherited capital He interprets the deporting agency as continuing God, though royal executive agency remains possible.
column3: Does the singular deported subject continue God or shift to the Assyrian king, and how should that distinction affect capitalization?

column2: Retain Levi's Gedson, Kaath and Merari within the selected chapter 5 boundary. The priestly genealogy is not renumbered into chapter 6 to match another edition.
Retain Kaath's Ambram, Issaar, Hebron and Oziel. Each selected name remains without normalization to a different English transliteration scheme.

Retain Ambram's sons heading including Mariam, and Aaron's four sons Nadab, Abioud, Eleazar and Ithamar. The gendered heading including a female name remains visible rather than silently becoming children.
column3: Should sons be broadened to children here because the Greek list explicitly includes Mariam, or should the source heading remain with a note?

column2: Retain Eleazar begetting Phinees and Phinees begetting Abisou. The repeated explicit begetting relation remains in the opening priestly chain.
Retain Abisou begetting Bokai and Bokai begetting Ozi. No collateral names are added from another priestly list.
Retain Ozi begetting Zaraia and Zaraia begetting Mariel. These selected forms are not replaced by different familiar priestly names.
Retain Mariel begetting Amariah and Amariah begetting Achitob. The second occurrence of similar names later in the chain is not grounds for deleting this generation.
Retain Achitob begetting Sadok and Sadok begetting Achimaas. The full two-link sequence remains.
Retain Achimaas begetting Azariah and Azariah begetting Joanan. The following Joanas spelling is not anticipated by silently altering this entry.
Retain Joanas begetting Azariah and the priestly service in Solomon's Jerusalem house. The selected Joanan/Joanas difference is preserved and the serving priest is contextually Azariah.
Retain Azariah begetting Amariah and Amariah begetting Achitob. Repeated names from earlier links remain rather than being treated as a copying error to correct.
Retain Achitob begetting Sadok and Sadok begetting Salom. The later Sadok is not automatically identified as the earlier one without genealogical review.
Retain Salom begetting Chelkias and Chelkias begetting Azariah. No office title is added to these names within the chain.
Retain Azariah begetting Saraias and Saraias begetting Josadak. The final generation leads into the exile notice without added regnal synchronization.

Retain Josadak going in deportation with Judah and Jerusalem by Nabouchodonosor's hand. The selected shorter wording has no newly explicit divine sending agent to import, and this unit closes chapter 5.
